title: BoLT: A Benchmark to Democratize Black-box Optimization Research for Expensive LLM Tasks
abstract: arXiv:2605.17000v2 Announce Type: replace-cross  Abstract: Optimization of LLM training and inference configurations, such as hyperparameters, data mixtures, and prompts, is critical to performance, but it is often approached heuristically in practice, leading to potentially suboptimal outcomes. By framing them as noisy, expensive, and derivative-free optimization problems, Bayesian optimization (BO) and other black-box optimization (BBO) methods offer a promising yet underexplored direction for principled, sample-efficient methods. However, LLM training and inference costs are prohibitively high for most of the BBO research community, and new methods are often only evaluated on synthetic test functions and small-scale datasets that fail to capture the challenges of modern LLM optimization problems. translated_title: BoLT：让面向昂贵LLM任务的黑盒优化研究平民化的基准测试
tldr: 该论文提出了BoLT——首个以LLM为中心的基准测试，通过解决LLM训练与推理成本过高的门槛问题，使黑盒优化（BBO）方法能够在真实现代LLM任务（如超参数、数据混合和提示词优化）上进行系统研究和平民化评估。
en_tdlr: The paper introduces BoLT, the first LLM-centric benchmark that democratizes black-box optimization (BBO) research by enabling principled, sample-efficient evaluation of methods on realistic LLM training and inference tasks, such as hyperparameter, data mixture, and prompt optimization.
